title: Undoing a function: Celsius to Fahrenheit and back

explain.say: It is 25 degrees Celsius in Mexico City, and your cousin in the USA asks: what is that in Fahrenheit? A function turns one into the other. Look at the first stage: we start at 25 degrees Celsius.

explain.say: Step one: multiply by 1.8. 25 times 1.8 is 45. See the second stage? Then step two: add 32. 45 plus 32 is 77 degrees Fahrenheit. Look at the third stage. That whole machine is the function f.

explain.say: Now your cousin tells you 77 Fahrenheit. How do you get back to Celsius? You run the machine backwards. Which step do you undo first, the multiply or the add?

stages.label: Start: 25 °C
stages.note: A warm day in Mexico City.

stages.label: + 32 → 77 °F
stages.note: Second step: add 32. That is f.

stages.label: Undo: − 32 → 45
stages.ask: Why do you undo the steps in reverse order?

stages.label: Undo: ÷ 1.8 → 25 °C

explain.say: The last step first! Like taking off shoes before socks. Undo adding 32 by taking away 32: 77 minus 32 is 45. Look at the fourth stage. Then undo multiplying by dividing: 45 divided by 1.8 is 25. The last stage!

explain.say: Back to 25 Celsius. Well done! That backwards machine is the inverse function, f inverse of x equals x minus 32 over 1.8. On a graph, a function and its inverse are mirror images in the line y equals x.

faq.a: An inverse function undoes what the function did. If f turns 25 into 77, then f inverse turns 77 back into 25.

faq.q: How do you find the inverse of a function?
faq.a: Write y equals f of x, then undo each step in reverse order to get x on its own. For y equals 1.8x plus 32, x equals y minus 32 over 1.8.
asks: How do I work out an inverse?

faq.q: Why do you undo the steps in reverse order?
faq.a: The last thing done is on the outside, so it must come off first, like putting on socks then shoes and taking off shoes then socks.

faq.q: Why are a function and its inverse mirror images?
faq.a: The inverse swaps every input and output, so the point a, b becomes b, a. Swapping x and y reflects the graph in the line y equals x.

faq.q: Does every function have an inverse?
faq.a: No. Only one-to-one functions do, where each output comes from just one input. y equals x squared sends 3 and minus 3 to 9, so it has no inverse unless you restrict it.
asks: When does a function have no inverse?

facts: The graph of an inverse function is the reflection of the original graph in the line y = x.

quiz.say: f of x equals 2x plus 3. What is f inverse of 11?

wrong.0: 25 applies f to 11 instead of undoing it.
wrong.1: 7 divides first, undoing the steps in the wrong order.

quiz.say: What is 50 degrees Fahrenheit in Celsius?

wrong.1: 27.8 divides by 1.8 without first taking away 32.
wrong.2: 122 converts the other way, Celsius to Fahrenheit.
